deliberation: One substantive Human Steward decision may authorize a finite set of deterministic administrative consequences only when every consequence is completely determined and execution contains no residual policy choice. The proposal is viable as a design direction, not as present merge or activation authority. Path allowlisting alone cannot make content administrative; governed-payload identity must include the authority-relevant dependency closure. Authorization identity and exact execution identity must remain separate but explicitly bound. Stage 1 may proceed within current routing powers, while any validity-rule or autonomous-merge change requires the effective amendment route and separate Human Steward action.
discharged_obligations: Exposed the primitive entities, assumptions, invariants, and authority boundaries.
Separated recommendation, deterministic execution, institutional effectiveness, production truth, and mathematical certification.
Identified the existing authority conflict that prevents immediate automated projection merging.
findings: Administrative projection needs a versioned semantic definition; path classification is insufficient.
Governed payload lacks normative canonicalization and dependency-closure rules.
Transition edges lack preconditions, postconditions, idempotency, ordering, expiry, and failure semantics.
Current authority prohibits automation from activating or exercising reserved human power.
Payload identity must not replace exact-base, generated-head, checks, and readback identity.
conditions: Define projections as byte-reproducible schema-constrained functions of immutable inputs.
Define a versioned governed-payload manifest whose unclassified changes fail closed.
Bind authorization to the matter, packet, payload, graph, exact edges, Human Steward, and supersession rule.
Complete Article XI requirements before autonomous merge authority is enabled.
Run shadow mode with zero tolerance for scope expansion, replay, bypassed holds, false activation, or evidence loss.
